newsitem.title: USA: Gennifer Flowers doubts Jones' sex harassment claim.
newsitem.headline: Gennifer Flowers doubts Jones' sex harassment claim.

text.p: Gennifer Flowers, another of President Clinton's female accusers, said Thursday she doubted that Clinton had sexually harassed Paula Jones and denied reports she would testify on Jones' behalf.

In an interview on "The Alan Colmes Show," a national radio talk show, Flowers said reports in USA Today and Time magazine that she would testify for Jones were false and that she had never spoken with either news organisation.

During the 1992 presidential campaign Flowers said Clinton had had a 12-year affair with her, prompting then-Arkansas Gov. Clinton to admit to "past indiscretions," although he adamantly denied any link to Flowers.
Jones has filed a sexual harassment suit against Clinton, accusing him of making unwanted advances toward her in 1991 in an Arkansas hotel room when he was governor and she was a state employee.

Clinton has denied the incident took place, although his private lawyer, Robert Bennett, Sunday acknowledged that Jones may have visited a business suite Clinton was using at the Excelsior Hotel on the day she alleges he exposed himself to her and asked her to perform oral sex.

"I find it hard to believe that he would sexually harass, in the true sense of the word, Paula Jones or anyone. I find it hard to believe that he would drop his pants and expose himself to someone who had not clearly let him know that's what she wanted him to do," Flowers said.
Flowers said she questioned the legitimacy of Jones' sexual harassment claims but said she should be entitled to a trial if she had legitimate evidence.

Referring to Jones' claim that she could identify a "distinguishing characteristic" of Clinton's anatomy to back up her claims, Flowers said, "I have no idea what she means by that. There is no mark there that I remember."
